# /onboarding/story-select

Step 4 of 7 in first-run onboarding, and the fork between two different ways
of telling the story behind the drawing. It is the point where the flow stops
being one straight line: one branch stays inside onboarding, the other leaves
it.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/onboarding/story-select` |
| Router file | `app/onboarding/story-select.tsx` |
| Flows | F2 First-run onboarding, F3 Invite and join |
| Position in flow | step 4 of 7, the typed/recorded fork |
| Data calls | none. No read, no write call |
| Shared surface | none of its own; the recorded branch hands off to `/record`, shared with F4 |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

## Features

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|-----------------|
| Choose to type the story, advancing to `/onboarding/story` | `app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:41-49` |
| Choose to record the story, advancing to `/record` | `app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:56-64` |

Both cards are plain `Pressable` buttons with no other affordance on the
screen: no back button, no skip. Not an omission in this write-up; the
affordance is absent from the source.

The two paths are not two on-ramps to the same next screen. Reading
`app/onboarding/story-select.tsx` in full:

- The typed card's `onPress` calls `router.push("/onboarding/story")`
  (`app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:45`). This is the branch that stays on
  the seven-step `ONBOARDING_STEPS` list (`src/lib/onboardingFlow.ts:11-19`).
- The recorded card's `onPress` calls
  `router.push({ pathname: "/record", params: { next: "onboarding-walls" } })`
  (`app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:60`). `/record` is `app/record.tsx`, the
  same recording screen F4's daily loop uses
  (`product/design/screen-flow-inventory.md`, F4 section). It is not on the
  onboarding step list at all. The `next: "onboarding-walls"` param is how
  `/record` knows to return into onboarding rather than into the daily
  `/choose-channels` step; `/onboarding/story` never enters this branch.

So "step 5 of 7 is `/onboarding/story`" is true only for the typed path. A
person who taps the microphone skips `/onboarding/story` entirely and is
routed through a screen that F2's own inventory entry does not list as one of
the seven onboarding routes. This is worth flagging on its own: the flow
diagram in `product/design/screen-flow-inventory.md` draws F2 as a single
straight line through all seven steps, and that line is only accurate for
half of this fork.

## Data calls

No call, no read. The screen renders static copy and two buttons; nothing on
this route reads from or writes to the API or a store, beyond the guard
described below.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** `useDraftStore.getState().imageRef`, read once inside a
mount effect to run the draft guard (`app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:25`).

**Writes on mount.** `useOnboardingStep("story-select")`
(`app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:19`) persists the step name to
AsyncStorage under a per-user key
(`src/lib/useOnboardingStep.ts:16-18`, `src/stores/useOnboardingStore.ts:220`).

**Writes on exit.** None from this screen. Nothing is written to a store
before either `router.push` call; the drawing already sits in `useDraftStore`
from the canvas step.

### The draft guard is enforced here, not only by resumeStep

`src/lib/onboardingFlow.ts:34` lists `story-select` in
`DRAFT_REQUIRED_STEPS`, and `resumeStep()` (`src/lib/onboardingFlow.ts:53-60`)
returns `"canvas"` for a draft-required step when there is no draft. But that
function is a resume calculation, called through
`useOnboardingStore`'s `resumeTarget` (`src/stores/useOnboardingStore.ts:246`)
at app launch, not from inside this component.

This screen enforces its own copy of the same guard. Reading
`app/onboarding/story-select.tsx` in full: a mount effect checks
`useDraftStore.getState().imageRef` directly and calls
`router.replace("/onboarding/canvas")` if it is falsy
(`app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:22-23`), with a comment naming the case it
covers: "deep link / cold resume". So the guard exists twice in the
codebase, once as the resume-time calculation in `onboardingFlow.ts` and once
as a component-level redirect in this screen (and, per its own file, in
`app/onboarding/story.tsx` and `app/onboarding/walls.tsx` the same way). They
are not the same code path.

## Components

| Component | Path |
|-----------|------|
| `OnboardingFrame`, the shared onboarding chrome and paragraph copy | `components/onboarding/OnboardingFrame.tsx`, imported at `app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:11` |
| `Icon` wrapping `lucide-react-native`'s `Mic` | `components/ui/icon.tsx`, `app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:12` |

No canvas, no shared drawing surface. This is the lightest screen in the F2
walk: two buttons and no state of its own beyond the guard.

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### The fork is asymmetric, and the wiki inventory undersells it

The screen-flow inventory draws F2 as `ob4 --> ob5 --> ob6 --> ob7`, one
line. That is the typed path. The recorded path leaves F2's own screen set
for `/record`, an F4 screen, before rejoining onboarding at `/onboarding/walls`
via a `next` param. Anyone using the inventory's flow diagram to reason about
what a new person actually sees will miss that half the fork takes a
detour through a screen built for the daily loop, with onboarding-specific
copy nowhere in sight once they land there.

### Two independent implementations of the same guard

The draft guard exists as a pure function (`resumeStep`) and, separately, as
a hand-written effect in at least three screens (`story-select.tsx`,
`story.tsx`, `walls.tsx`, per the comment pattern each carries). A person
extending the draft-required step list has two places to change it, and
nothing enforces that they stay in sync beyond convention and the tests in
`tests/onboardingFlow.test.ts`. Worth deciding whether the per-screen guard
should call `resumeStep`/`resumeTarget` instead of re-checking `imageRef`
directly.

### No skip, no back, and that is a real product question

There is no way out of this screen except forward. For a POC that is a
reasonable default, but it means a person who taps the wrong card cannot
back out of the recording flow to reconsider typing instead, short of
whatever back-stack behavior `/record` itself provides. Not verified here;
out of scope for this page, but worth a line in the F2 workflow page.
